title: Brandade
subtitle: A warm salt cod and potato puree from the south of France
excerpt: Salt cod soaked overnight, then simmered and worked with potato, olive oil, and warm milk into a silky puree. Serve warm with toast or crudites.
sourceNotes: Provencal and Languedoc tradition, with roots in the broader Mediterranean salt cod repertoire.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to one month. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently, adding a splash of warm milk to loosen.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a large saucepan for the soaking and cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Brandade keeps in the fridge for three days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over a low heat, stirring, with a little extra olive oil or milk.

content.text: Brandade is a thick, creamy puree of salt cod and potato. The cod must be soaked for at least 24 hours to draw out the salt. Add the oil slowly so the mixture stays cohesive and does not become greasy.

items.prepNote: soaked in cold water for 24 to 48 hours, changing the water three times
floury variety, peeled and cut into chunks

content.text: Drain the soaked cod and place in a saucepan with the garlic. Cover with cold water. Bring to a very gentle simmer and poach for 10 minutes. Do not boil or the fish will toughen.
At the same time, cook the potato in a separate pan of unsalted water until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well and mash until smooth.
Lift the cod from the water and discard the skin and any bones. Pull the flesh into rough flakes. Place in a warm bowl with the garlic cloves.
Warm the olive oil and milk separately in two small pans or heatproof jugs. They should be warm, not hot.
Mash the cod and garlic together. Add the potato and stir to combine.
Gradually work in the warm oil and milk, alternating between the two, beating with a wooden spoon or spatula. The mixture should be thick and smooth.
Season with lemon juice and pepper. Taste before adding any salt. Serve warm with toasted baguette.

items.symptom: The brandade is still very salty after soaking.
items.cause: The water was not changed often enough, or the cod was not soaked long enough.
items.fix: Soak for a further 6 to 8 hours with fresh water, tasting a small piece before cooking.

items.symptom: The mixture is greasy and the oil has separated.
items.cause: The oil was added too quickly or too cold.
items.fix: Beat vigorously and add the oil in a very slow, thin stream, as if making mayonnaise.

items.symptom: The texture is gluey rather than fluffy.
items.cause: The potato was overworked after adding the fish.
items.fix: Mash the potato on its own first, then stir the fish in gently rather than beating hard.
